title: Deep learning designs Muller glia-specific regulatory elements validated in mouse retina
summary: Deep-learning chromatin-accessibility models designed compact cis-regulatory elements predicted to be Muller glia-specific in human and mouse, with accessibility driven by creation of LHX2 motifs. In vivo, the designed elements restricted reporter expression to Muller glia in the murine retina. The number of constructs and specificity quantification were not reviewed; this is a preprint.
ai_technology: Deep-learning chromatin-accessibility models for cis-regulatory element design

evidence.tested: In vivo reporter expression testing in murine retina.
evidence.unknown: Specificity across constructs, performance in human tissue and use in gene therapy vectors; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning models designed the regulatory sequences before in vivo testing.
